title: Find Eventual Safe States
summary: Given a directed graph with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, where each node points to its adjacent nodes, identify all nodes that lead to a terminal node or another safe node through every possible path.
statement: Given a directed graph with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, where each node points to its adjacent nodes, identify all nodes that lead to a terminal node or another safe node through every possible path. Return these safe nodes in ascending order.
constraints: Nodes are 0 through n-1 in a directed graph.
A node is safe when every possible path from it eventually ends; return safe nodes sorted.
reference_solution:
def eventual_safe_nodes(graph):
    state=[0]*len(graph)
    def safe(node):
        if state[node]:return state[node]==2
        state[node]=1
        if all(safe(following) for following in graph[node]):state[node]=2;return True
        return False
    return [node for node in range(len(graph)) if safe(node)]

def eventual_safe_nodes(graph):
    state=[0]*len(graph)
    def safe(node):
        if state[node]:return state[node]==2
        state[node]=1
        if any(safe(following) for following in graph[node]):state[node]=2;return True
        return False
    return [node for node in range(len(graph)) if safe(node)]
hints: A node is unsafe if DFS reaches a currently visiting node or any unsafe successor.
Use three colors: unseen, visiting, and proven safe.
Mark visiting; recursively require every neighbor safe; then mark safe.
A visiting revisit detects a reachable cycle, while completed safe nodes memoize paths already proved terminating.
